title: Horus Telemetry Daily Event Volume
dataSources: APRS packets (`aprs:packet`), WSPR spots (`wspr:spot`), satellite passes (`satpass:prediction`), NOAA APT captures (`noaa:apt`), meteor-scatter pings (`meteorscatter:ping`), SSTV images (`sstv:image`).
app: Software-defined radio and ham stations — APRS igate, WSPR beacon, NOAA weather-satellite (APT) receiver, meteor-scatter monitor, and SSTV decoder — logging to Splunk HEC via scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=horus:telemetry
| bin _time span=1d
| stats count as events, dc(payload_id) as distinct_entities by _time
| sort - _time
description: Counts how many Horus telemetry events land each day and how many distinct payload values are represented.
value: Daily volume is the fastest way to spot a dead feed, a sudden burst, or a workflow that quietly changed.
implementation: Ingest Horus telemetry records into `index=personal`; schedule daily and compare count and distinct payload values against your normal baseline.
visualization: Column chart of daily event count with a line for distinct entities.
grandmaExplanation: It reviews how much Horus telemetry activity showed up each day so you can see if the feed went quiet or suddenly got busy.
